coverage.creator_scope: Attribution-context IDs, not a census of unique people or verified speakers.

methods.lexical: Shared masked unigram/bigram TF-IDF; log TF, smoothed IDF, L2, min_df2, max24,000 features; negation retained.

neural.token_pooling: Attention-mask mean including CLS/SEP, then chunk L2 normalization
neural.document_pooling: Content-wordpiece-weighted mean of normalized chunks, then document L2 normalization
neural.cache: Exact ordered input/model/pooling/code bindings in private RAM; no model weight updates
neural.batch_order: Content length descending, then original chunk ordinal

methods.topic_model: Fixed eight-factor NMF, random starts at seeds11/23/47, max500 iterations. Topic-term components scaled to unit L2 with compensating W columns; mixtures and progression use this fixed factor scale. Labels are top lexical terms.

hypotheses.question: Do lexical and neural neighborhoods agree under one canonical frame?
hypotheses.limitation: Agreement between representations is not agreement between answers.

hypotheses.question: How stable are neural neighborhoods under a bounded text window?
hypotheses.limitation: Windowing changes content and length together; no causal length effect.

hypotheses.question: Does source context remain enriched among neighbors after availability correction?
hypotheses.limitation: Channels, formats, creators and themes are confounded.

hypotheses.question: Do fixed-eight lexical factors remain stable across numerical seeds?
hypotheses.limitation: Stability does not validate a topic ontology or justify eight factors.

hypotheses.question: Do same-name cross-creator messages outrank different-name within-creator messages in the four preselected Mary/Magdalene texts?
hypotheses.metric: Within-context minus cross-context mean cosine across full/bounded lexical/neural views
hypotheses.limitation: Two dependent pairs per side; source style, length and topic are confounded. Names are printed attributions, not authenticated beings.

limitations: Purposive retained English-source frame; missing historical captions and undiscovered uploads are outside the denominator.
Canonical publications, text editions, recordings, creators, channels and claimed entities are distinct. Exact deduplication does not establish independent ideas.
Machine transcripts have unverified word accuracy and speaker roles. Source selection and format can dominate similarities.
Document pairs are dependent; no pairwise p-values, real-world probabilities, predictive forecasts or automatic agreement labels are reported.
Name masking is incomplete. Frequent terms, repeated introductions, paraphrases, spelling and writing style remain possible explanations.
Pretrained MiniLM is a reproducible lightweight baseline, not a new SOTA or trained model. Topics, embeddings and graphs describe text representations.

execution.scope: Measured runtime and input coverage, not a recognition/semantic accuracy benchmark or causal speedup estimate.

creator_comparison.scope: Equal canonical-document weights within named-creator contexts. Creator attribution does not identify every interview utterance; 13 guest-publisher contexts do not become 13 independent mediums.

lexical.scope: Different declared balancing units, not alternative estimates of an authenticated-medium population. Pairs remain dependent.

semantic.scope: Different declared balancing units, not alternative estimates of an authenticated-medium population. Pairs remain dependent.

term_overlay.selection: Top24 non-name unigrams by equal-publisher-context mean TF-IDF; document frequency≥3 and context frequency≥2. Exact name-component terms excluded; fixed alphabetical ties.
term_overlay.units: Mean L2-normalized document TF-IDF weight within each publisher context, not topic prevalence.

projection.scope: One PCA on normalized term vectors transforms every channel-term mean. A normalized term prototype need not sit at the plotted source-point average.

contextual_terms.sampling: At most two documents per publisher context/term, selected by SHA256(term|canonical source ID); one middle ordinal occurrence per document. Mean target subwords in ±24-wordpiece contexts; normalize occurrence, mean within context, then equal-context term mean and normalize.
limitations: Sentence-trained MiniLM target-token states are exploratory, not validated word senses or new trained word embeddings.
The bounded deterministic sample is not representative of every use. Spelling, grammar and source style can dominate proximity.
Balancing is by publisher context, not independently authenticated people; guest-publisher contexts are not new mediums.
Shared coordinates and token cosines do not imply common answers, contradictions or identity of claimed entities.
